verses.1: Come down and sit on the ground, O virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called tender and delicate.
verses.2: Take the millstones, grind the flour. Remove your veil, uncover your thighs, bare your legs. Cross the rivers.
verses.3: Your nakedness will be exposed, your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance and will not give it to another.
verses.4: The LORD of Hosts is your redeemer, holy is his name, the God of Israel.
verses.5: Sit in silence, enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called the strength of kingdoms.
verses.6: I was angry with my people, I defiled my inheritance. I gave them into your hand. You showed them no mercy, you greatly burdened the old.
verses.7: And you said, "I will reign forever." You did not consider these things in your heart, you did not remember your end.
verses.8: Now listen to this, you delicate one, who dwells securely, who says in your heart, "I am, and there is none other. I will not sit a widow, I will not know the loss of children."
verses.9: Yet two things will come upon you in a moment, in a single day— loss and widowhood. They will come to you as surely as you relied on your sorceries and the might of your counselors.
verses.10: You trusted your evil, saying, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and knowledge have brought ruin. You said in your heart, "I am, and there is none other."
verses.11: Yet ruin will come upon you that you do not know. A disaster will fall upon you that you cannot atone for. A sudden calamity will come upon you that you do not foresee.
verses.12: Now stand in your enchantments and in your many sorceries with which you have learned since your youth. Perhaps you may gain advantage, perhaps you may ward off disaster.
verses.13: You have labored in your counsel. Let now the astrologers of the heavens, who watch the stars and declare the new moons, rise up to rescue you.
verses.14: Behold, they are like stubble, fire will burn them. They cannot save their lives from the flame. There is no coal for baking bread, no fire to warm them.
verses.15: So are those who have been your merchants since your youth. Each one goes astray for his own ruin. There is no savior for you.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: The rendering of "holy is his name" follows the context of God's identity and the use of "name" to denote divine character.
- v. 9: "Loss and widowhood" reflects the Hebrew terms sh'khol and alman, which are used in parallel to signify complete devastation.
- v. 14: The metaphor of stubble and fire is retained to capture the imagery of utter destruction in the original.
raw:
[1] Come down and sit on the ground, O virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called tender and delicate.

[2] Take the millstones, grind the flour. Remove your veil, uncover your thighs, bare your legs. Cross the rivers.

[3] Your nakedness will be exposed, your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance and will not give it to another.

[4] The LORD of Hosts is your redeemer, holy is his name, the God of Israel.

[5] Sit in silence, enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called the strength of kingdoms.

[6] I was angry with my people, I defiled my inheritance. I gave them into your hand. You showed them no mercy, you greatly burdened the old.

[7] And you said, "I will reign forever." You did not consider these things in your heart, you did not remember your end.

[8] Now listen to this, you delicate one, who dwells securely, who says in your heart, "I am, and there is none other. I will not sit a widow, I will not know the loss of children."

[9] Yet two things will come upon you in a moment, in a single day— loss and widowhood. They will come to you as surely as you relied on your sorceries and the might of your counselors.

[10] You trusted your evil, saying, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and knowledge have brought ruin. You said in your heart, "I am, and there is none other."

[11] Yet ruin will come upon you that you do not know. A disaster will fall upon you that you cannot atone for. A sudden calamity will come upon you that you do not foresee.

[12] Now stand in your enchantments and in your many sorceries with which you have learned since your youth. Perhaps you may gain advantage, perhaps you may ward off disaster.

[13] You have labored in your counsel. Let now the astrologers of the heavens, who watch the stars and declare the new moons, rise up to rescue you.

[14] Behold, they are like stubble, fire will burn them. They cannot save their lives from the flame. There is no coal for baking bread, no fire to warm them.

[15] So are those who have been your merchants since your youth. Each one goes astray for his own ruin. There is no savior for you.

---
Notes
- v. 4: The rendering of "holy is his name" follows the context of God's identity and the use of "name" to denote divine character.
- v. 9: "Loss and widowhood" reflects the Hebrew terms sh'khol and alman, which are used in parallel to signify complete devastation.
- v. 14: The metaphor of stubble and fire is retained to capture the imagery of utter destruction in the original.
